pr_body:
Addresses a condition where making nested calls to `JsonSerializer` can result in `JsonException` metadata being overwritten by the outer serializer. The serializer will now recognize exception instances where `JsonSerializer.Path` is already populated and bubble them up without any modification (treating them like any other exception type).

Fixes #51537.

issue_context.title: System.Text.Json: Preserve JsonException.Path
comments:
This seems to be caused by the following two catch blocks: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ddaa1c3c503f989db48102f50a693765e4e6ae2a/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/JsonConverterOfT.WriteCore.cs#L50 and https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ddaa1c3c503f989db48102f50a693765e4e6ae2a/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/JsonConverterOfT.ReadCore.cs#L94

This is catching any `JsonException` exceptions and overwriting the `Path` property. Perhaps we should be using the [`ReThrowWithPath`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ddaa1c3c503f989db48102f50a693765e4e6ae2a/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/ThrowHelper.Serialization.cs#L331) method instead? cc @steveharter @layomia

review_comments: This checks NullOrEmpty while the new catch only checks for null, so there is a semantic change here

Note that the catch clause will check if `JsonException.Path` is null, not the exception message.

I changed this particular line because the method consuming the `AppendPathInformation` property will [turn it on regardless for null or empty message strings](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e9268fbe638687c32db49f90ee0f05f6ddd3f62b/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/ThrowHelper.Serialization.cs#L361), so the existing branching is redundant.
